fileStructure: app/reset.py: token issuance, validation, and confirmation for password reset. app/models.py: User gains no new field. app/auth.py: unchanged; login remains the only session source. app/mailer.py: unchanged.

tasks.title: ResetToken record and single-use token issuance
tasks.produces: ResetToken dataclass (token, user_id, expires_at, used); create_token(user_id: int) -> str; token_row(token: str) -> ResetToken | None
tasks.specExcerpt: R1 — Token issuance. A reset token is a random 32-hex-character string bound to one user id, valid for 30 minutes, single-use. Storage is a dict keyed by the token string; an expired or unknown token is indistinguishable to a caller.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_token -v → OK (3 tests): a fresh token is 32 hex chars, token_row returns the row for it, and token_row returns None for an unknown string
steps: write tests/test_reset_token.py asserting len(create_token(1)) == 32 and all chars in string.hexdigits
run it → ModuleNotFoundError: app.reset
add app/reset.py with the ResetToken dataclass and a module-level _TOKENS dict
implement create_token using secrets.token_hex(16) and a 30-minute expires_at
implement token_row as a dict lookup returning None on miss
run it → OK (3 tests), commit

tasks.title: request_reset issues a token and mails the link
tasks.specExcerpt: R2 — Requesting a reset. `request_reset(email)` looks the user up, issues a token, and mails a link. An address with no account is accepted silently — the response must not reveal whether an account exists.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_request -v → OK (2 tests): a known address appends one entry to mailer.sent whose body contains the issued token, and an unknown address returns None while leaving mailer.sent empty
steps: write tests/test_reset_request.py for both the known and unknown address
run it → AttributeError: request_reset
implement request_reset: store.get_user_by_email, early return on None, create_token, mailer.send_email
run it → OK (2 tests), commit

tasks.title: Reset email body: expiry and one link
tasks.consumes: the token string produced by create_token
tasks.specExcerpt: R3 — The email. The mail body names the expiry in minutes and carries the reset link exactly once. Copy is plain text; no HTML part.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_email -v → OK (2 tests): the body contains '30 minutes' and body.count('/reset/confirm?token=') == 1
steps: write tests/test_reset_email.py asserting the ttl string appears and the link appears exactly once
run it → AttributeError: reset_email_body
implement reset_email_body as an f-string; have request_reset call it
run it → OK (2 tests), commit

tasks.title: validate_token rejects expired, unknown, and used tokens
tasks.consumes: token_row and the ResetToken.used/expires_at fields from app/reset.py
tasks.specExcerpt: R4 — Validating a token. `validate_token(token)` returns the token row for a live token and nothing for an expired, unknown, or already-used one.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_validate -v → OK (4 tests): live token returns the row; unknown, expired (expires_at backdated), and used (used=True) each return None
steps: write tests/test_reset_validate.py covering all four cases
run it → AttributeError: validate_token
implement validate_token: token_row, then reject on used or expires_at in the past
run it → OK (4 tests), commit

tasks.title: confirm_reset writes the new credential and consumes the token
tasks.produces: confirm_reset(token: str, new_password: str) -> bool — sets User.password_hash via auth.hash_password, marks the token used, saves the user
tasks.consumes: validate_token from app/reset.py; hash_password from app/auth.py; save_user from app/store.py
tasks.specExcerpt: R5 — Setting the new password. Given a live token and a new password, the account's stored credential becomes that password, the token is consumed, and the user can immediately sign in with it. `app/auth.py:login` reads `User.password_hash`; that is the field a successful reset has to leave behind.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_confirm -v → OK (3 tests): confirm_reset returns True, store.get_user(1).password_hash == auth.hash_password(new_password), and the token row has used=True
steps: write tests/test_reset_confirm.py asserting the stored hash equals hash_password(new_password)
run it → AttributeError: confirm_reset
implement confirm_reset: validate_token, user.password_hash = auth.hash_password(new_password), row.used = True, store.save_user
run it → OK (3 tests), commit

tasks.title: A completed reset clears a failed-attempt lockout
tasks.produces: confirm_reset additionally clears User.locked_reason when it equals 'failed-attempts'
tasks.consumes: confirm_reset from app/reset.py; User.locked_reason from app/models.py
tasks.specExcerpt: R6 — Lockout interaction. A reset clears `User.locked_reason` when it was set by failed sign-in attempts, so a user is not locked out of the account they just recovered.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reset_lockout -v → OK (2 tests): after confirm_reset, store.get_user(1).locked_reason is None for 'failed-attempts' and still 'fraud-review' for the other
steps: write tests/test_reset_lockout.py asserting locked_reason for both reasons
run it → the fraud-review case passes, the failed-attempts case fails
add the conditional clear inside confirm_reset before save_user
run it → OK (2 tests), commit
